 The honor of serving you is not something I take lightly, and I do so with even more energy and resolve than I had four years ago.
 We will continue to serve you with professionalism and a relentless pursuit of justice, working every day to ensure we keep Hamilton County the greatest place to live, work, and play.
 Thank you for your steadfast support, confidence, and the trust you place in me. It’s the honor of a lifetime to serve as your sheriff, and I look forward to continuing to lead and serve alongside the incredible men and women of your Sheriff’s Office.”
 - Sheriff Austin Garrett

 Hamilton County, TN – On the evening of August 31, 2026, an HCSO deputy initiated a traffic stop at the intersection of Mowbray Pike and Millsaps Road.
 The motorcyclist failed to stop, initiating a pursuit that ended at the 9800 block of Indian Ridge Trail, where the suspect, identified as Douglas Sluder, was taken into custody.
 Sluder faces the following charges: 
 • Evading Arrest
 • Reckless Endangerment 
 • Driving Under the Influence 
 • Driving on a Revoked License
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

We're celebrating leadership across Hamilton County in #EastRidgeTN! 👏🏼
 City of East Ridge Administration and Elected Officials were proud to attend the Hamilton County Government Elected Officials Swearing-In Ceremony this morning at the Chattanooga Convention Center.
 On behalf of the City of East Ridge, we congratulate all of Hamilton County’s newly elected and returning officials who took the oath of office and committed themselves to serving the residents of our community.
 East Ridge is especially proud to recognize the leaders who represent our city and District 8, including Hamilton County Commissioner Josh Wichman, and School Board Member Katie Perkins.
 As East Ridge and the greater Hamilton County community continue to grow, strong partnerships between our local governments, schools, community leaders, and elected officials remain essential to moving our region forward! 
 We look forward to this next chapter of leadership and to continuing our work together in support of the residents, businesses, families, and communities we collectively serve.
 Congratulations to all who were sworn in today, and best wishes for a successful term of public service!

items.content_text:
Africa is already experiencing the impacts of climate change, yet key data on climate policies remain limited or unavailable across the continent. 
 This makes it harder for governments to design effective climate policies and target action where it is needed most. 
 A new report by the #OECD, GGGI, the World Bank and OECD's Sahel and West Africa Club helps close these information gaps. It brings together data on climate risks and climate policies across 28 African countries, using the #OECD Climate Actions and Policies Measurement Framework. 
 The report shows that:
 ➡️Climate policy action in Africa has more than doubled between 2010 and 2024, but have slowed down significantly from 2021 onwards.  
 ➡️Africa already experiences the most severe droughts across all continents, indicating risks to agriculture. 
 ➡️A very high-emissions scenario could lead to a doubling of hot days across the continent by 2100.
 Explore the report: https://brnw.ch/21x5lRG

Message From Your Sheriff - Flock/ Motorola LPR Cameras Paused
 As of today, I have directed staff within your Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office to begin the process of pausing the Flock License Plate Recognition (LPR) and Motorola LPR programs managed by our Office. 
 This directive, being weighed over several weeks, encompasses multiple factors that have contributed to this decision. 
 The primary factor is the tremendous concern regarding public data and potential misuse of what is captured. 
 Within the HCSO program, your Sheriff’s Office oversees approximately 70 cameras across Hamilton County.
 As your elected Sheriff, I truly believe in LPR technology and its ability to combat criminal activity in Hamilton County and those criminals who are here to cause harm and turmoil.
 At my direction, HCSO Command Staff will continue to work through factors of concern that led me to this decision to pause until I am confident that all areas of these concerns are addressed. 
 During this time, I call on our state and federal leaders to begin a conversation into what is best for our state, our country, and the protection of the citizens of Hamilton County.

HCSO Recovers Homemade Explosives, Weapons, Stolen Property
 Hamilton County, TN – On August 28, 2026, the HCSO Criminal Investigations Unit conducted a controlled buy on Facebook Marketplace with a suspect who posted stolen items two days prior. A joint operation was then launched involving the HCSO Criminal Investigations Unit, Narcotics and Special Operations Unit, alongside Uniformed Services deputies.
 HCSO detectives and patrol deputies initiated a traffic stop on Hixson Pike, where the suspect was found in possession of the stolen property. Deputies executed a search warrant at the suspect’s home and three storage units, where deputies located drugs, drug paraphernalia, a loaded 9mm handgun, an altered shotgun, an altered flare gun, a large quantity of ammunition, two explosive military hand grenade simulators, 15 homemade explosives, and approximately $40,000--$60,000 in stolen property.
 The stolen property has been linked to multiple thefts and burglaries being investigated by the Hamilton County Sheriff's Office and the Chattanooga Police Department.
 The suspect, James Robert Bowman, was taken into custody and faces the following charges:
 • Prohibited Weapons x17
 • Felon in Possession of a Firearm x3
 • Burglary
 • Theft of Property
 The HCSO would like to thank the Chattanooga Police Department Bomb Squad and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) for their assistance in this investigation.
 Additional charges are pending in relation to the investigation. This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

There’s more than 130 years of history behind the doors of one of UTC’s most distinctive buildings. 🏛️
 Built in 1896, the Isbester House at 551 Oak St. was once the home of Chattanooga industrialist Caleb B. Isbester. Over the years, the historic Queen Anne Revival home served as a mayor’s residence, a men’s dormitory and professional offices before returning to UTC in 2011.
 Following extensive restoration and preservation, the building became known as Alumni House in 2016. Today, it serves as an administrative headquarters for campus, housing the offices of the chancellor, provost and director of economic and workforce development.
 🔗  Discover the story behind one of UTC’s historic landmarks and the people who helped shape Chattanooga: https://blog.utc.edu/…/if-these-walls-could-talk-alumni-ho…/

🍎 Teacher Highlight: Mr. Wood | Thrasher Elementary

For 26 years, Mr. Wood has been making an impact in the classroom, including more than two decades at Thrasher Elementary. As a fifth-grade math teacher, he has found a way to make learning active, engaging and something students can look forward to.

Mr. Wood loves finding creative ways to bring math to life. One project his students look forward to is designing and building tiny houses. Students create a blueprint, use what they’ve learned about volume and work together to build their own tiny house models, combining math with hands-on learning and STEM.

But for Mr. Wood, teaching is about much more than academics. It’s about getting to know his students and creating a classroom where they feel comfortable being themselves. From talking sports to trading Pokémon cards and playing music, he looks for those small moments that help build relationships and make his classroom feel like a place where students belong.

He also loves helping students discover that math doesn’t have to be intimidating. Seeing a student go from believing they “hate math” to feeling confident in what they can do is one of the most rewarding parts of his job.

After more than two decades at Thrasher, Mr. Wood says his students continue to keep him young, keep him learning and keep him coming back ready to make a difference.

And if his students leave his classroom smiling, a little more confident and ready for what comes next, Mr. Wood considers that a good day.

Tax revenue is the income a government receives through taxes, such as personal income tax, corporate income tax, taxes on goods and services.
 The latest Revenue Statistics in Asia and the Pacific report highlights how tax revenues evolved across the region in 2024.
 ➡️ The average tax-to-GDP ratio rose to 19.7%, marking the fourth consecutive annual increase.
 ➡️ Personal income tax revenues increased by 0.3 percentage points (p.p.) of GDP on average across the region, while corporate income tax revenues rose by 0.1 p.p.
 ➡️ Tax revenues increased in 16 economies, with the largest rises in the Cook Islands (+5.9 p.p.), Mongolia (+4.8 p.p.) and the Marshall Islands (+4.7 p.p.).
 ➡️ Tax-to-GDP ratios ranged from 6.7% in Bangladesh to 33.7% in Japan.
 ➡️ Over the last decade, tax-to-GDP ratios increased in 23 Asia-Pacific economies and declined in 15.
 These findings show how economic developments and changes in income tax revenues continued to shape domestic resource mobilisation across the region.
 Read the full Revenue Statistics in Asia and the Pacific report:️ https://brnw.ch/21x5ki0

 Justin has been busy at the Police Department working with Red Bank Aluminum to install a new 30' x 17' vehicle shelter for the Special Operations Unit. The previous shelter was simply too small and didn’t provide complete coverage for the vehicle.
 The good news? The old shelter isn’t going anywhere! It will remain in place and be used to protect smaller vehicles.
 We’re always looking for ways to improve our facilities, protect our city assets, and better support our team. Small projects like this make a big difference!
 Thanks to Justin and the Red Bank Aluminum team for helping us get it done! 👏
 #WhereInRedBank #RedBankTN #RedBankPolice #CityImprovements #CommunityFirst

August 31st is International Overdose Awareness Day.
 During this observance, we honor those we have lost to overdose, support individuals and families impacted by substance use, and raise awareness about the importance of prevention and education. Recognizing the signs of an overdose and knowing how to respond can make a life-saving difference. 
 If you or your community group want to learn more and help save lives, please schedule a training with the Hamilton County Coalition by calling 423-305-1449.
 Please visit https://www.cdc.gov/stop-overdose/response/index.html for more information.

This is what community looks like! ❤️🌳🚵
 An incredible 75 volunteers showed up to support our trails alongside SORBA Chattanooga. We are so grateful for every person who gave their time, energy and hard work to care for these special outdoor spaces.
 Thank you, SORBA Chattanooga—and thank you to every volunteer who continues to make Hamilton County parks and trails better for everyone!
 #HamiltonCountyParks #SORBAChattanooga #TrailCommunity #VolunteerPower #ParksForEveryone
75 volunteers showed up on a Saturday morning for the final Trail Daze of Summer Work Party at Walden's Ridge Park! It was epic and the largest trail work party EVER!!
 Partnering with SCC, SORBA-Chattanooga, and Hamilton County Tennessee Parks and Recreation Department, trained crew leads broke everyone into teams and we touched almost every trail in the system.
 🧗 SCC crews tackled boulder approach trails + a major rock project
 🚵 SORBA crews cleaned up the downhill + traverse trails
 Thank you to every single person who showed up to get dirty and sweaty for these trails! We made a big impact and we couldn't have done it without each of you! 🙌
 Want to give back too? Join us as a volunteer or member. It takes a village to care for 100 miles of trail.
 📅 Next up: September 18 with Booker T. Washington State Park
 🔗 Link in bio for our calendar of events
 #SORBAchattanooga #SCC #TrailStewardship #WaldensRidge  #TrailDazeofSummer

🧐🤔Reflecting on this week….💙
 As a City Council representative and community leader, it has always been my intent to represent every part of District 7, while understanding that the work is always bigger than any one district.
 First and foremost, I thank God for the opportunity to serve. It is a privilege I don’t take lightly, and I’m incredibly grateful to represent such an amazing constituency.
 The pictures I’m sharing are just a few of the stories and investments happening across District 7—investments that are making our district stronger and positioning Chattanooga for an even stronger future.
 My team and I keep up with these stories, but more importantly, we keep up with the people and the conversations behind them.
 Because community work is not always easy, but it is absolutely worth it—and it is NEVER done in silos.
 And whether I’m showing up to support an initiative, sitting in another meeting, working through an idea with community, or literally taking orders at the register at Cocoa Cafe 😂☕️—I’m in the work! I believe leadership means being present, being accessible, and being willing to roll up your sleeves and serve wherever I’m needed.
 When you see the work, just know there are tons of people behind it. People who have workshopped ideas with me, attended countless meetings, asked tough questions, offered different perspectives, and yes… even told me, “That’s not a good idea.” 😂
 And I appreciate every single one of them.
 Because without my community, I wouldn’t be able to do this work for the betterment of OUR community.
 The good.
 The bad.
 The ugly.
 And the beautiful.
 All of it is part of the work. All of it matters. And all of it is part of Building Stronger Communities. 💪🏾🏙️❤️
 Cheers to continuing to do this work—together. 🥂🏾
 And yes… sometimes that means City Councilwoman by day, barista by afternoon. 😂☕️

items.content_text:
River City Company's Emerging Producers: Where are they now?
 Pedro Abriles, a 2024 Emerging Producers program graduate, has kept busy between community work, composing and producing music, and sound production for a variety of events. Pedro's most recent project involves the transformation of a well-known Chattanooga landmark: the vacant Parkway Towers building beside Highway 27, known for decades as simply "the Junk Building" for its graffitied rooftop billboard that now reads "Love."
 The new "Love" mural is the result of a partnership between Pedro and singer-songwriter, Steve Derthick, whose third album Pedro was producing. Pedro was motivated to find a way to change the old billboard from "Junk" to a more positive message for people driving through the city. "What if instead of junk, the billboard said something hopeful, like love?" The two had just finished recording Derthick's newest song, "City of Love."
 When Pedro was able to secure permission from the owners of Parkway Towers, he enlisted the help of local artist and creative strategist Rondell Crier for the planning of the mural and an accompanying creative engagement experience that allowed the community to contribute to the artwork. Volunteers from Noah's Painting completed the mural, and members of the community were invited to paint 36 wooden hearts in memory of loved ones that would later be installed on the billboard.
 The project was filmed by cinematographer Christian Eaves to be featured in the music video for Steve Derthick's song, "City of Love." We are incredibly proud of Pedro for facilitating such an impactful project, and we look forward to following his future work! 
 Watch the music video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SeORVaCHMq0

items.content_text: Monday is International Overdose Awareness Day. According to the CDC, overdose deaths in the U.S. decreased nearly 14% from 2024 to 2025. That's definitely progress, but there's still work to do! If you're interested in learning more about resources and recovery, you can attend "Gathered in Grace". This free event includes overdose response training, survivor testimonials, and recognition for officers who've helped save people from overdosing. It's Monday (8/31/26) from 2:00pm-5:00pm at Abba's House (5208 Hixson Pike).

items.content_text:
For children five and under, books beat screens when it comes to learning.  
 The latest International Early Learning and Child Well-being Study shows that regularly reading books to children continues to be one of the most important learning activities that families can do - but it is not always that common. 
 In some jurisdictions, fewer than half of households read to their five-year-olds more than three times a week.  
 Read the report to learn more about the importance of parental activities and other actions that have the most positive impact:
